# Safety classes {#safety-classes}

Every tool in the catalogue carries a safety classification in the
manifest. The classification decides how the tool is surfaced — what
runs by default, what asks before firing, what stays behind an
explicit opt-in.

| Class | Meaning | Default posture |
|---|---|---|
| `safe` | self-contained; no live firing | installable and runnable normally |
| `requires-target` | fires requests at a target system | runs only when given an explicit target; refuses to self-fire |
| `exp` | experimental code execution surface | gated behind the lab-mode wrapper contract; opt-in only |

The default-off posture for the `exp` class is a design decision
recorded as an architecture decision record in the OS repository
([the safety-defaults record](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/spec.md#92-safety-defaults-module-basesafety-defaultsnix)):
no `exp`-classified tool becomes reachable through menu or CLI
defaults, and the wrapper contract that emits a lab-mode shell is
generated from the manifest like every other surface.

## Responsible use

The distribution ships offensive AI-security tooling alongside
defensive and platform tooling, built for **authorised security work
only**: engagements with written authorisation, academic research, and
defender-validation against systems the operator is authorised to
test. Possession of a tool is not authorisation to use it. The full
statement — the operator's responsibilities and the named legal
provisions per jurisdiction — lives at
[the responsible-use page](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/responsible-use.md)
and is mirrored into every Layer-ATTACK surface of the distribution.

Safety class is also surfaced on every generated reference page in
[Part III](../reference/coverage.qmd), so a reader always sees the
posture of a tool before its invocation forms.
